key_terms.meaning: A legal upper limit on the mass of each pollutant (CO, HC, NOx, PM) that a vehicle may emit per kilometre, measured on a fixed test cycle
Matching families of emission norms; Bharat Stage VI limits are given in g/km and are enforced on every new vehicle sold in India
The air-to-fuel mass ratio at which fuel burns completely, about 14.7:1 for petrol
λ = actual air-fuel ratio ÷ stoichiometric air-fuel ratio; λ = 1 means chemically correct, λ < 1 rich, λ > 1 lean
The turning moment the engine delivers at the crankshaft, measured in N·m; T = brake power ÷ angular speed
Usable power at the crankshaft, P = 2πNT/60 with N in rev/min and T in N·m, giving P in watts
Brake specific fuel consumption = fuel mass flow rate ÷ brake power, in g/kWh; lower is better
A lookup table of the best control values, such as injection time and spark advance, indexed by speed and load
Electronic control unit: a microcontroller that reads sensors, looks up maps and drives actuators many times per second
Control in which the ECU measures the result (here exhaust oxygen) and corrects its output to remove the error
Control from stored maps only, with no feedback; used when the sensor is cold or at full load
Computing trapped air mass per cylinder from inlet manifold absolute pressure, inlet air temperature and engine speed, using volumetric efficiency from a map
Exhaust gas oxygen (lambda) sensor; its voltage switches sharply near λ = 1 and tells the ECU whether the mixture is rich or lean
The time in milliseconds for which the ECU holds the injector open; fuel mass is proportional to it
Actual air mass drawn into the cylinder divided by the mass that would fill the swept volume at inlet conditions; it sets the fuel to be injected
The time the ignition coil primary current is switched on to build energy before the spark; too short gives a weak spark, too long overheats the coil
A piezo accelerometer on the block that detects the characteristic high-frequency vibration of detonation so the ECU can retard timing
Exhaust gas recirculation: a measured part of the exhaust is fed back to the inlet to lower peak combustion temperature and cut NOx
A converter that oxidises CO and HC while reducing NOx, and needs the mixture to stay within a narrow band around λ = 1

takeaways: Each new emission stage lowers the legal ceiling per kilometre, and only close mixture and spark control can meet it.

Air-fuel ratio is a compromise: rich mixtures give power and cool the exhaust, lean mixtures give economy but raise NOx, and λ = 1 is the only point where a three-way catalyst works on all three pollutants at once.
Torque is the twisting effort, power is torque multiplied by speed, and BSFC tells you how much fuel each unit of that power costs.
An ECU replaces mechanical feel with stored maps indexed by speed and load, so the same engine can hold different compromises at every operating point.
Electronic fuel control estimates trapped air per cylinder, converts it to injector open time, then trims that time using the exhaust oxygen sensor.
Spark timing and dwell are set digitally, and the knock sensor lets the ECU run close to the knock limit without damaging the engine.
Sensors, actuators, the ECU and the in-vehicle network together form the engine management system that diagnostics, traction control and cruise control all read from.
bank_note: Long answers are almost always built on the chain: sensor, ECU map and actuator, with the effect of air-fuel ratio, spark timing and EGR on emissions, power and BSFC shown as the justification for electronic control.

bank.q: Define brake specific fuel consumption and derive its relation with fuel mass flow rate and brake power. Explain why BSFC is a better yardstick than fuel flow alone.
outline: BSFC = fuel mass flow rate ÷ brake power, units g/kWh
Power from torque and speed: P = 2πNT/60
Fuel flow from injector pulse width, number of cylinders, injections per cycle and fuel density
Two engines drinking the same litres per hour but making different power are not equally efficient
Lowest BSFC occurs at moderate speed and high load; show the BSFC islands on the engine map

bank.q: Explain the working of a three-way catalytic converter and why the engine must be held near λ = 1 for it to work.
outline: Oxidation of CO and HC and reduction of NOx happen together over platinum, palladium and rhodium
The catalyst is most efficient inside a narrow window around stoichiometric mixture
Rich mixture leaves CO and HC unconverted; lean mixture lets NOx pass
Closed-loop control with the EGO sensor keeps switching across λ = 1 in that window
Ceramic honeycomb coated with washcoat; light-off temperature and cold-start problem

bank.q: Distinguish open-loop and closed-loop fuel control. State when the ECU switches between them.
outline: Open loop: fuel from stored map only, no feedback
Closed loop: EGO sensor output trims the injection duration
Sensor behaves as a switch around λ = 1; short-term and long-term trims
Open loop used during cold start, warm-up, full load enrichment, high speed and sensor failure
Fail-safe running from maps if the sensor fails

bank.q: Explain the speed-density method of estimating the air trapped in a cylinder.
outline: Inputs: manifold absolute pressure, inlet air temperature, engine speed, volumetric efficiency from a map
Ideal gas relation gives air density in the manifold
Air mass per cycle = density × swept volume × volumetric efficiency
Charge per cylinder = mass per cycle ÷ number of cylinders; for four stroke divide by two revolutions
Not suitable without correction for backflow and for variable valve timing; contrast with mass airflow sensing

bank.q: Explain dwell and the electronic ignition control sequence for one cylinder.
outline: Coil stores energy when primary current flows; spark at switch-off by induced high voltage in secondary
Dwell is the charging time; energy = ½LI², so dwell must suit battery voltage and speed
ECU computes dwell from speed and battery voltage; constant energy dwell control
Spark advance from speed-load map, corrected for coolant temperature and knock
Skip-spark and misfire detection via coil current sensing

bank.q: Trace how emission norms have tightened from Euro I to Euro VI or BS I to BS VI and state what each step demands from the engine management system.
outline: Limits are given in g/km for CO, HC, NOx and PM and are measured over a fixed drive cycle
Progressive cuts, especially in NOx and PM for diesel
Demands: precise fuel metering, closed loop λ control, better mixing, high pressure injection, EGR, converters and particulate filters
On-board diagnostics and monitoring of emission components
Link between tighter limits and the need for electronic rather than mechanical control

bank.q: A four-cylinder four-stroke petrol engine runs at 3000 rev/min with a measured air mass flow of 30 kg/h and λ = 1. Stoichiometric ratio is 14.7. Each injector fires once per cycle. Fuel density 750 kg/m³. Find the fuel flow, the mass of fuel per injection and the injector open time if the injector flows 2 g/s when open.
outline: Fuel flow = 30 ÷ 14.7 = 2.04 kg/h
Injections per second = 4 × (3000/60) ÷ 2 = 100 per second
Fuel per injection = 2.04 kg/h ÷ 3600 ÷ 100 = 5.7 mg
Open time = 5.7 × 10⁻³ g ÷ 2 g/s ≈ 2.8 ms
Comment on dead time and battery voltage correction

bank.q: An engine develops 60 kW brake power at 4000 rev/min and consumes 18 kg of petrol per hour. Calculate brake torque, BSFC and brake thermal efficiency. Take calorific value of petrol as 44 MJ/kg.
outline: BSFC = 18000 g/h ÷ 60 kW = 300 g/kWh
Fuel power = 18/3600 × 44 × 10³ kW = 220 kW
Brake thermal efficiency = 60 ÷ 220 ≈ 27 per cent
Note the inverse relation between BSFC and efficiency

bank.q: Explain how the ECU uses the knock sensor to protect the engine, and show with a step-by-step sequence how spark timing changes when knock appears.
outline: Knock is auto-ignition of end gas, producing a ringing vibration at a known frequency band
Sensor is a piezo accelerometer; signal is filtered and windowed to the knock window after each spark
Retard timing in small steps until knock stops, then advance slowly back
Retard limited to a safe value; if knock continues, enrich mixture or limit boost
Trade-off: retarded timing raises exhaust temperature and worsens BSFC

bank.q: Describe how air-fuel ratio affects exhaust emissions, fuel economy and power, and explain how the controller chooses the compromise at idle, part load and full load.
outline: Rich: CO and HC rise, NOx falls, power rises, economy falls
Lean: CO and HC fall, NOx peaks then falls with very lean, economy improves, power falls, misfire risk
λ = 1 closed loop for part load to feed the three-way catalyst
Slight enrichment at full load for power and component protection
Cold start enrichment and fast idle; deceleration fuel cut-off
Trade-off shown on an emissions versus λ curve

bank.q: Compare carburetion with electronic petrol fuel injection on mixture accuracy, cylinder-to-cylinder distribution, emissions, cold starting and transient response.
outline: Carburettor meters fuel by air velocity and venturi depression; errors from viscosity, temperature, wear and altitude
Port injection meters fuel per cylinder by open time, independent of manifold behaviour
Transient response: wall wetting and fuel film compensation need electronic control
Cold start and altitude correction from maps and sensors
Explain why BS VI levels cannot be reached with a carburettor

bank.q: Evaluate the effect of EGR on NOx, knock, combustion stability and fuel consumption, and explain how the ECU meters EGR.
outline: NOx forms at high peak temperature; EGR dilutes the charge and lowers peak temperature
Moderate EGR also suppresses knock, allowing more advance
Too much EGR causes misfire and higher HC and CO; idle and full load need little or none
Metering by stepper motor valve, vacuum operated valve or electronic throttle; feedback from EGR position and manifold pressure
Cooled EGR and its effect on volumetric efficiency

bank.q: A car has a fault in the manifold absolute pressure sensor. Analyse how the ECU detects the fault and what fallback strategies keep the car running.
outline: Plausibility checks: signal range, comparison with throttle angle, speed and airflow models
Circuit checks for open and short to ground or supply
Fallback from a substitute value, often throttle-based or a default manifold pressure
Fixed spark advance, open-loop fuel, limited engine speed and disabled EGR
MIL lamp, diagnostic trouble code stored, freeze-frame data, read over CAN by a scan tool

bank.q: Draw the block diagram of an engine management system and explain the role of each block, including the in-vehicle network and diagnostics.
outline: Inputs: crank position, cam position, MAP, air temperature, throttle angle, coolant temperature, EGO, knock
ECU blocks: input conditioning, ADC, microcontroller, maps in memory, output drivers
Outputs: injectors, coils, idle air or electronic throttle, EGR valve, canister purge, fuel pump relay
Closed loop around EGO and around idle speed
CAN bus links ECU, transmission, ABS and body modules; diagnostics and limp-home modes

glossary.def: Mass of air divided by mass of fuel entering the engine, about 14.7 for complete combustion of petrol.
Actual air-fuel ratio divided by the stoichiometric ratio; 1 means chemically correct.
The mixture strength at which all fuel can burn using all the oxygen supplied.
A charge in which fuel vapour and air are fully mixed before ignition.
Ratio of air actually trapped in the cylinder to the swept volume filled at inlet conditions.
Pressure inside the inlet manifold measured against vacuum, used with speed to estimate trapped air.
An electrically opened valve that sprays atomised fuel; the quantity delivered is set by open time and pressure difference.
The time in milliseconds an injector stays open, commanded by the ECU.
The short part of an injector pulse, roughly 0.5–1 ms, in which the injector has opened but fuel flow has not reached full rate.
Time the ignition coil primary is energised before the spark.
Crank angle before top dead centre at which the spark occurs, chosen from a speed-load map.
Uncontrolled auto-ignition of the end gas after the spark, producing a sharp pressure rise and metallic sound.
Correction the ECU applies to injection time from the oxygen sensor, kept as short-term and long-term learning.
A valve that admits a controlled fraction of exhaust gas into the inlet to lower combustion temperature.
A converter that oxidises CO and HC and reduces NOx together when the mixture stays near stoichiometric.
A two-dimensional table of calibrated control values indexed by speed and load.
The process of filling those tables by testing the engine on a dynamometer and choosing values that meet emission and driveability targets.
The computer that runs the maps in real time and drives the actuators.
A sensor, usually magnetic or Hall effect, that reports crankshaft position and speed to the ECU.
A voltage appears across a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field; used in position and speed sensors.
A two-wire broadcast bus with message identifiers and arbitration that lets vehicle modules share data.
A stored code that identifies which monitored circuit or system has failed.
A fallback strategy in which the ECU uses substitute values so the car can be driven slowly to a workshop.
Brake power divided by the heat energy supplied by the fuel.
